title: Backend: rehydrate jobs from disk at startup
description: jobs is a process-local dict in create_app. A server restart empties /api/jobs, 404s every job URL, and orphans completed models that are sitting on disk in the session folder with meta.json and output/. Deep-linking and resumability are impossible until this is fixed. Scan root/*/meta.json at startup and reconstruct job records, deriving status from the presence of output/model.glb.
acceptance_criteria: After a server restart, GET /api/jobs lists prior sessions and GET /api/jobs/{id} returns 200 with its artifacts.
close_reason: Delivered in be1b31b + 382313b. 319 tests pass; verified in headless Chromium against a real job.

title: Video-to-frames ingest so the photogrammetry regime is reachable
description: The >=16-photo ORBIT regime is the only path that measures geometry, but shooting 40 deliberate stills is a real barrier and every run so far has fallen into the generative regime with 4-5 photos. ffmpeg is now on worker v5; wire an ingest path that accepts a short orbit video and extracts evenly spaced sharp frames (drop blurry ones using the existing quality assessment in ingest/quality.py). Thirty seconds of orbit video is a far easier capture than forty stills.

title: Single-view generation picks its conditioning photo by filename order
description: On the single-view path the backend uses images[0] after _select_conditioning_views, which with untagged photos is simply the alphabetically first filename. For a single-view generation that ONE photo determines the entire model, and the user has no way to choose or even see which it was until reading result.json. Demonstrated on the tetrapod: the good 2026-08-03 run was conditioned on 'WhatsApp Image ... 02.47.16 (1).jpeg' and a later run on 'WhatsApp Image ... 02.47.16.jpeg' - a different photo - purely because the (1) file was absent from the second upload and the sort order shifted. Expose a primary-view picker, and log which photo conditioned the model.
close_reason: Shipped in 206769c. Seeds are auto-generated, used, and recorded in job settings and result.json; rerun inherits them; --seed added to the CLI. The pipeline now names the photos that actually conditioned the model and how many were unused. Implemented by an agy engineer with three defects corrected by the master before integration - notably it had cut TRELLIS conditioning from 4 images to 1.

title: Pin a generation seed so a good result is reproducible
description: TRELLIS is stochastic and PixieCAD passes seed=None, so quality is a lottery: the same 4 photos and identical settings produced fill 0.966 on one run and 0.047 (an unusable blob) on the next. There is no way to reproduce a good result or to A/B a setting change, because the seed varies underneath. Expose a seed in the dashboard, record the seed actually used in session.json, and default a rerun to the seed of the run being rerun.
close_reason: Shipped in 206769c. Seeds are auto-generated, used, and recorded in job settings and result.json; rerun inherits them; --seed added to the CLI. The pipeline now names the photos that actually conditioned the model and how many were unused. Implemented by an agy engineer with three defects corrected by the master before integration - notably it had cut TRELLIS conditioning from 4 images to 1.

title: Two concurrent TRELLIS jobs deadlock the worker
description: Launching a second generative job while one is in flight wedges kngsly/trellis2-worker: both requests reached 'Sampling sparse structure: 100%' and then stopped dead. Observed 2026-08-08: two ESTABLISHED /generate connections to the container, /ready returning HTTP 000 after 20s (event loop blocked), GPU 0% across samples, process State I(idle) with 0.23s CPU over 40s, and 14 minutes of log silence. The worker holds one pipeline on one GPU and cannot serve two generations. PixieCAD must refuse or queue a second generative job against the same host rather than letting the user wedge it. There is also no cancel endpoint - both jobs run in one 'pixiecad serve' process, so a single job cannot be stopped without restarting the server.
close_reason: Guarded in 455caf4: _register_and_dispatch returns 409 when another running or queued job holds the same gpu_host. Follow-up filed for the missing per-job cancel.

title: TRELLIS runs the hd profile at 2M faces; A/B against game_ready
description: The worker picks mesh_profile=hd when nothing is set, which is what every run so far has used: geometry_resolution 1024, decimation_target 2,000,000, texture 4096. That is the likeliest source of the 40,341-component confetti mesh. PIXIECAD_TRELLIS_MESH_PROFILE now selects the profile and the job's face budget now reaches decimation_target, but the A/B has not been run. Also: microsoft/TRELLIS-image-large (the original MIT TRELLIS) is already cached on the host at 3.1 GB, but kngsly/trellis2-worker hardcodes Trellis2ImageTo3DPipeline, so loading it needs a different worker image.

title: HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 breaks texturing when a repo is not in the baked cache
description: Offline mode was added so a HF CDN outage could not break a job that needs nothing from HF. But it is absolute: the paint multiview repo is not in this image's cache, so snapshot_download raises LocalEntryNotFoundError and texturing fails outright. Offline should be a preference that falls back to the network on a genuine cache miss, not a hard wall.
close_reason: Fixed in d3a2f22: SDF surface extraction replaces binary marching cubes; HF offline now falls back to the network on a genuine cache miss, and the missing Hunyuan3D-2.1 weights (14 GB) are cached on the host.

title: Solidify's marching cubes terraces every curved surface
description: Solidify extracts its surface from a BINARY voxel grid, so curved regions come out as 45-degree staircase steps while flat regions (which land on grid planes) look clean. Measured on the shipped model: 4.2% of edges sit at exactly 45 degrees and 0.0% fall in the 5-20 degree band a real curved surface would produce. User reports 'flat faces get solidified better and the curved ones are still like a mesh'. Fix: extract from a smoothed signed distance field instead.
close_reason: Fixed in d3a2f22: SDF surface extraction replaces binary marching cubes; HF offline now falls back to the network on a genuine cache miss, and the missing Hunyuan3D-2.1 weights (14 GB) are cached on the host.

title: Rerun a finished or failed job with one click
description: A failed job holds everything needed to retry it: the staged photos in input/ (already renamed to carry view tags) and its settings. Nothing surfaced that. After an infrastructure failure -- stale SSH key, missing rtree -- the only way back was to re-upload the photos and re-pick every option. Persist the settings to session.json so a restored job can be rerun too, add POST /api/jobs/{id}/rerun, and put a button on the job detail screen.
close_reason: Shipped: POST /api/jobs/{id}/rerun creating a new session from the original's photos and settings, settings persisted to session.json so restored jobs are rerunnable, shared _register_and_dispatch with create_job, and controls on the job detail header plus every terminal row in the jobs list. 7 tests, verified end to end against a live server.

title: Worker image was missing rtree, killing the bake and the whole job
description: trimesh calls ProximityQuery.on_surface -> nearby_faces -> mesh.triangles_tree -> rtree, so the normal-map bake needs rtree even though nothing imports it directly. pixiecad-hunyuan in worker-v2 did not have it. The bake raised, and because unwrap and bake shared one try block the pipeline discarded a finished 969k-face mesh that had cost 333s of L4 time.
close_reason: Fixed in c85fb72. rtree installed into the live host image and into setup_hunyuan_vm.sh; launch_from_image.sh self-heal generalised to check_dep covering fast_simplification and rtree. Separately, unwrap and bake are no longer in one try block, so a bake failure can never discard a finished mesh again.

title: A GPU backend that cannot be reached must say why
description: A stale SSH HostKeyAlias in ~/.ssh/config (VM recreated, same name and IP, new instance id) made ssh fail host-key verification. RemoteHunyuanBackend.available() catches Exception and returns False, and SSHExecutor.probe() discards ssh stderr, so the job log said only: "Backend 'hunyuan-remote' is not available. Registered backends: ['fake','hunyuan-remote','trellis-remote']" -- which reads as a wrong backend NAME and sends you looking in the wrong place. The fix (gcloud compute config-ssh) was one command once the cause was visible. Surface the real reason: unreachable + ssh stderr, no GPU detected, or insufficient VRAM.
close_reason: Fixed in 95fcac3: Capabilities.detail + why_not(), probe() keeps ssh stderr, _ssh_hint() names the fix, available() records last_unavailable_reason, get_backend() prefers it over the registry dump. 15 new tests. The triggering incident was resolved by 'gcloud compute config-ssh' after the VM was recreated.

title: Texture stage: missing fast_simplification in the paint image
description: Sixth dependency failure in the Hunyuan paint stack. hy3dpaint/utils/simplify_mesh_utils.py calls trimesh.simplify_quadric_decimation, which in trimesh 4.x delegates to fast_simplification rather than a built-in. The package was never installed, so texturing dies with ModuleNotFoundError after the pipeline has already loaded (~15s GPU time) and the job finishes untextured with only a WARNING. Fixed in scripts/setup_hunyuan_texture.sh; the currently-baked machine image still lacks it and needs a rebake.
acceptance_criteria: A texture job on a freshly built image completes and reports 'Texture applied.'
notes: VM pixiecad-gpu self-destructed before the fix could be applied: launch_from_image.sh sets --max-run-duration=7200s with --instance-termination-action=DELETE, so every VM and its 200GB disk are deleted after exactly 2 hours. Nothing left to rebake from. Mitigation: launch_from_image.sh now checks the paint image for fast_simplification on every launch and patches it in place (~20s) if missing, so a stale machine image degrades to a slower launch rather than silently broken texturing. Rebake opportunistically during the next session, before the 2h timer.
close_reason: Fixed three ways: added to setup_hunyuan_texture.sh for future builds, self-healing patch in launch_from_image.sh for stale images, and baked into pixiecad-worker-v2. Verified in the image: fast_simplification 0.1.13.

title: Dashboard never writes output/model.glb
description: A completed dashboard run leaves only model_web.glb and parts/ in output/. The publish step copies the pipeline's glb (named <spec>.glb, e.g. tetrapod.glb) to output/model.glb, and finishing then rewrites it, but no job has ever produced that file. The full-resolution model is therefore only reachable inside work/ws/output/. Reproduce with a dashboard run and trace the publish block against finish_model's out_dir.
close_reason: Not reproducible: current code writes output/model.glb correctly (verified with a fake-backend run producing model.glb + model_web.glb + parts). My original diagnosis printed job['glb_path'], a field get_job never returns - it exposes glb_url. Kept a files API that lists output/ from disk so this class of confusion cannot recur.

title: Semantic part segmentation via multi-view 2D segmentation
description: Hunyuan output is a single fused shell (99.96% of area in one connected component), so connected-component splitting finds nothing and the pipeline falls back to k-means clustering, which carves arbitrary spatial blobs instead of semantic parts. Fix: render the mesh from N angles with a face-ID buffer, segment each RGB render with SAM on the GPU host, back-project masks to faces via the ID buffer, and fuse labels across views by voting.

title: Untagged photos silently drop Hunyuan to single-view
description: map_views matches view tags by filename substring, so untagged photos (IMG_2841.jpeg, WhatsApp Image ....jpeg) match nothing, view_map comes back empty and the run falls back to single-view Hunyuan 2.1 conditioned on images[0] - chosen by filename sort order. The other photos are ingested and counted in the log ('4 accepted') but never touch the geometry, and nothing warns. The code comment at web/app.py:738 acknowledges the silent fallback. Should say in the job log which photos actually conditioned the model and that the rest were unused. Related trap: substring matching means 'leftover-shot.jpg' maps to left and 'backyard.jpg' maps to back.
close_reason: Shipped in 206769c. Seeds are auto-generated, used, and recorded in job settings and result.json; rerun inherits them; --seed added to the CLI. title: Watertight check should weld by position before judging
description: A Hunyuan model with ZERO holes reports watertight=False and 9,130 open edges, because xatlas duplicates vertices along every UV seam (14,709 stored vertices for 10,002 distinct positions) and is_watertight counts edges by vertex index. Welding by position gives 0 open edges and identical volume. The warning is a false alarm that sends the user looking for a leak that does not exist. Weld positionally before reporting, and report genuine non-manifold edges separately.
close_reason: Fixed in 0e390ed. check_mesh welds by position before counting edges, and reports holes vs non-manifold pinches separately. Implemented by an agy coder; master corrected one defect - the worker made pinches flip report.ok, which the pipeline maps to a FAILED sanity stage, so a good Hunyuan model (1 pinch, 0 holes) would have failed.

title: Emit per-part pivots and hinge axes for animation
description: Parts already share world coordinates (trimesh.submesh does not recentre), so dropping every part GLB into a scene at identity reconstructs the model - the one property an anime.js scroll animation needs. But Part.centroid and Part.extents are computed in segment.py and DROPPED at the export_parts boundary; manifest.json carries no bbox, centroid, transform or parent/child relation, and export_glb wraps every part as a single node named 'model' with identity transform. To rotate a lighter lid you need a hinge axis, which nothing derives - it is obtainable by fitting a line to the shared edge loop between two adjacent parts. Add centroid/bbox to the manifest and derive a hinge axis per adjacent part pair.

title: Each part GLB embeds a full copy of the texture atlas
description: webexport.py:9-18 documents it: parts keep the whole model's UV layout, so every part file carries the entire atlas even though it uses a fraction of it. _shrink_parts mitigates by downscaling per part, but a 13-part scroll animation still downloads the same texture 13 times. Needs UV repacking or a per-part rebake.

title: No way to cancel a single running job
description: All jobs run inside one 'pixiecad serve' process and there is no cancel endpoint, so stopping one job means killing the server and losing every other in-flight job. Surfaced during the 2026-08-08 TRELLIS deadlock: the user wanted one of two jobs stopped and the only option was a full server restart.

title: Docker-created cache files are root-owned, breaking the TRELLIS token write
description: Containers run as root, so files docker creates in ~/.cache/huggingface are root-owned, and a machine image bakes that in. trellis_remote copies an HF token to ~/.cache/huggingface/token as the SSH user and fails with 'Permission denied' -- a message that says nothing about ownership. Fixed on the live host and self-healed at launch in launch_from_image.sh. A better fix is running the containers with --user, or keeping the token outside the shared cache.

value: PixieCAD generative quality is a LOTTERY because no seed is pinned. Measured 2026-08-08: the same 4 photos, same settings, same trellis-remote backend produced extents [0.738,1.002,0.371] solidifying to fill 0.966 on one run, and extents [0.233,0.503,0.392] solidifying to only 0.047 on another - a blob. Diagnostic that separates 'bad generation' from 'bad tuning': re-run solidify on the saved raw mesh at work/ws/stages/s3-generate-*/out/mesh.glb. If a known-good mesh still reaches 0.95+ with current code, solidify is fine and the generation is the problem. No dilation rescues a bad one (6->0.047, 8->0.067, 10->0.137, 14->0.204). Since fbfbdf5 solidify marks fill<0.35 as repaired=False and the stage reports FAILED instead of ok.

PixieCAD solidify must extract its surface from a SIGNED DISTANCE FIELD, never a binary voxel grid. Binary marching cubes puts every vertex on a voxel corner, so flat faces (which lie on grid planes) look clean while curved ones become 45-degree staircases -- the exact user complaint 'flat faces get solidified better, curved ones still like a mesh'. Diagnose with the dihedral histogram: the tell is a spike at exactly 45 deg plus an EMPTY 5-20 deg band. Fix measured on a real 1.87M-face TRELLIS mesh: distance_transform_edt(~g)-distance_transform_edt(g), gaussian_filter sigma=1.5 VOXELS (resolution-independent), marching_cubes at level=-dilate (this replaces binary_erosion). 45-deg edges 4.2%->0.0%, mean dihedral 3.20->0.82, fill 0.958->0.969, surface moves only 0.09% of object size at p95. MUST nudge the level by -1e-4: an unsmoothed EDT is integer-valued along axes so an integer offset hits ~10k samples exactly, giving degenerate cells and a NON-watertight mesh. skimage index space matches trimesh VoxelGrid.marching_cubes exactly, no half-voxel shift.

S0 ingest is nowhere near needing cloud offload: the entire local pipeline (ingest, clean, decimate, UV unwrap, normal bake, parts export) peaks at 247 MB RSS in 1.9s on 8 1024px images. Only S2b dense stereo and S3 generative need a GPU host.

TRELLIS.2 requires an HF token: it loads facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m which is a GATED repo. The 401 only surfaces AFTER downloading 19GB and several minutes of loading, so always check the token before provisioning. Accept licence at huggingface.co/facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m, then export HF_TOKEN.

Two shared refcounted polling stores (lib/vm.ts, lib/jobs.ts) - never add a third poll of the same endpoint. Verify UI changes with chrome-headless-shell from ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright (--dump-dom + --screenshot); it has NO WebGL, so the 3D viewer always takes its no-WebGL fallback path there.

Part segmentation on a fused generative mesh: render 14 views keeping a face-id buffer, run SAM per view, vote on mesh EDGES (agree minus disagree across views), then Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher with k/area to form regions. Two designs failed first: clustering masks (SAM splits a wheel into rim+tyre in one view -> 90+ fragments) and cut-then-merge-by-mean-agreement (snowballs, one region went 13.6%->97.9%). Adjacency MUST be UV-seam-aware (_positional_face_adjacency); mesh.face_adjacency left 390 regions with no neighbour. SAM vit_h on a T4 = 125s for 14 views at 768px.

PixieCAD remote shell generation: NEVER pass a command to a shell wrapper as a string to eval. hf_run originally did 'eval $1' so the text was parsed TWICE; shlex.quote only defeats the first parse. Measured: a staged filename of photo'.glb was neutralised (quotes pair inside the literal) but photo$(touch /tmp/PWNED).glb EXECUTED, because command substitution is inert to the first parse and live to the second. Filenames are staged as 00<suffix>/mesh.glb but the SUFFIX is user-controlled and photo$(...).glb is a legal filename. Correct pattern, and BOTH halves are required: (1) the wrapper takes a FUNCTION NAME and re-invokes with "\$@" -- a function body is parsed once at definition, so deferred vars like $HF_OFFLINE still resolve late while user data is never re-parsed; (2) the arguments are still shlex.quote'd, because a function body EXPANDS at call time even though it parses once. tests/test_finishing.py parameterises 12 payload shapes over both generated scripts.

PixieCAD solidify had an exact off-by-half-a-voxel bug: scipy distance_transform_edt measures CENTRE TO CENTRE, so a voxel touching background gets edt==1 while sitting only 0.5 from the interface. The signed field is therefore sign*(d+0.5) and marching cubes at level -n lands at true depth n-0.5 -- half a voxel too far out per side, at EVERY resolution and dilation. Worth exactly +1.000 voxel of extent on an exact binary slab. Fix is two in-place lines after building the field: field[field>0]-=0.5; field[field<0]+=0.5. Side effect: gaussian blur then stops moving the surface at all (blurring a true SDF preserves level sets) - sigma 0 vs 1.5 agreed to 0.000 after, differed by 0.28 before. At offset==0 the +-1 samples bracket the interface symmetrically so the error vanishes, which is why an index-space alignment test against trimesh never caught it. Second term: voxelize marks the nearest centre so the shell protrudes uniformly in [0,1) voxels, mean 0.5, cancelled by SHELL_BIAS=0.5. Real-world result: thinnest axis went +8.52% -> +0.13%.

PixieCAD: the TRELLIS worker (kngsly/trellis2-worker) serves ONE job at a time and a second concurrent /generate DEADLOCKS it rather than queueing. Signature, measured 2026-08-08 with two jobs 55s apart: both reach 'Sampling sparse structure: 100%' then stop dead; /ready returns HTTP 000 after 20s (event loop blocked); GPU 0% across samples; worker process State I(idle) with ~0.23s CPU per 40s; two ESTABLISHED connections to 172.17.0.2:8000. Only recovery is 'docker rm -f pixiecad-trellis' and both runs are lost. Guarded since 455caf4: _register_and_dispatch returns 409 if another running/queued job shares the same gpu_host. Note there is still NO per-job cancel -- all jobs run in one 'pixiecad serve' process, so stopping one means restarting the server.

PixieCAD worker image v5 (baked 2026-08-09, 108.6 GB) = v4 + colmap/colmap:latest (8.75 GB) + ffmpeg. v1 and v4 DELETED after auditing v1 and confirming it was a strict subset of v4 (hunyuan, hunyuan-paint, sam, 9.2 GB weights). v5 is the only machine image. Photogrammetry split: sparse SfM runs LOCALLY via pycolmap (4.1.1, in the sfm extra), dense MVS runs on the host via docker colmap/colmap:latest - the exact tag geometry/dense.py hardcodes as DOCKER_COLMAP_IMAGE. Verified after bake: NVIDIA L4 visible inside the colmap container and FeatureExtraction.use_gpu present, so it is a CUDA build. To audit a machine image cheaply you must use a g2 machine type - overriding to e2 fails with 'features are not compatible' because the image carries the nvidia-l4 accelerator.

Spot is a bad fit for the TRELLIS leg specifically: ~15min cold start (9GB image pull + 19GB model download) and preemption DELETEs the boot disk, losing the whole cache. One run was preempted 8 min in. COLMAP dense is fine on spot because it is short and the stage cache absorbs a restart.

Normal-map baking is the heaviest local stage in PixieCAD by two orders of magnitude. Measured 2026-08-04 on the 16GB M3 against a 1.31M-face source decimated to 20k: 512=6.0s/1.76GB, 1024=13.6s/3.4GB, 2048=52.9s/4.1GB, versus ~247MB for every other local stage combined. Profiling: the mesh itself is only 321MB; essentially all of it is ONE call, trimesh ProximityQuery.on_surface, and CHUNKING THAT QUERY DOES NOT HELP (peak stayed 6.5GB) -- do not retry that. Fix was to move the work: bake_location=auto|local|host, with meshops/bake_remote.py running the same bake.py inside the hunyuan container. Payload is compressed .npz (11.7MB), NOT .glb -- a GLB round-trip must carry UVs through TextureVisuals and losing them yields a plausible but wrong map. The remote bake does NO GPU work (runs without --gpus); it is remote CPU. Never yet run against a real GPU host.

PixieCAD GPU worker cache reality (checked 2026-08-08): the baked machine image does NOT hold every repo. Present: microsoft/TRELLIS.2-4B 16G, tencent/Hunyuan3D-2mv 9.2G, microsoft/TRELLIS-image-large 3.1G, facebook/dinov3-vitl16 1.2G, PramaLLC/BEN2 363M. MISSING until 2026-08-08: tencent/Hunyuan3D-2.1 (14G) which BOTH single-view shape gen and the paint/texture stage need -- every textured job had been downloading it live, and the HF CDN 500 that motivated HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 was that download failing, not a spurious revision check. So HF_HUB_OFFLINE must be a preference with a network fallback on LocalEntryNotFoundError, never an absolute. Now fetched into the host cache; a v4 image rebake should capture it.

The TRELLIS image is built with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=8.9 and no +PTX, so it ships Ada cubins only. A T4 (7.5), A100 (8.0) and H100 (9.0) all fail at kernel launch regardless of VRAM. L4 is the required GPU; availability checks must test compute capability, not just VRAM.

TRELLIS load-time host RAM: OOM-killed at 15.2GB on g2-standard-4 (16GB); still climbing past 28GB on g2-standard-8 (32GB). Use g2-standard-16 (64GB). Adding swap makes it worse - paging a model load onto pd-balanced wedges the VM entirely.

TRELLIS worker image kngsly/trellis2-worker is a FastAPI SERVICE (CMD python server.py, EXPOSE 8000), not a CLI. Protocol: GET /ready, POST /generate multipart with repeated 'images' fields returning an NDJSON stream whose last frame carries success+glb_path, GET /download/<name>. Bind-mount /outputs to read the glb straight off the host instead of downloading it.

kngsly/trellis2-worker takes a mesh_profile that PixieCAD never set, so every run silently used its default 'hd': geometry_resolution 1024, decimation_target 2,000,000, texture_output_size 4096. That is why jobs came back at 1,872,364 faces regardless of the user's budget. The alternative is 'game_ready' (512 / 300,000 cap / 2048). Knobs the worker accepts: mesh_profile, geometry_resolution, decimation_target, texture_generation_mode, texture_output_size, steps, preprocess_image, post_scale_z, and TRELLIS2_MODEL_ID env (default microsoft/TRELLIS.2-4B). Loading microsoft/TRELLIS-image-large via TRELLIS2_MODEL_ID will NOT work: worker.py hardcodes Trellis2ImageTo3DPipeline and the original TRELLIS pipeline.json declares TrellisImageTo3DPipeline.

The fal.ai backend was REMOVED on 2026-08-04 (pixiecad-cag). It offered hosted TRELLIS.2 with no VM/L4/gated-weights, but only by uploading the user's photos to a third party -- the exact thing building Hunyuan from Tencent's own source was meant to avoid. It had never produced a model here. AUTO_PRIORITY is now [hunyuan-remote, trellis-remote]; there is no hosted backend and no FAL_KEY anywhere. tests/test_web.py::TestBackendSelection::test_no_third_party_hosted_backend_is_offered asserts none can reappear in the registry or the auto order, because the failure mode is silent: a job would just start uploading.

PixieCAD: never call mesh.voxelized() on a large mesh - it subdivides the WHOLE mesh until every edge is under half a voxel and holds it all at once. Measured on a 1.9M-face input at 256 divisions: 2.6 GB in that single call, 65% of solidify's entire footprint, and it was what made running at full resolution unaffordable on the 16 GB machine. meshops/solidify.py:_voxelize does the same thing 4000 faces at a time for 311 MB, producing a bit-identical grid; end-to-end solidify went 3.91 GB -> 2.06 GB. Use max_iter=20 on subdivide_to_size - trimesh defaults to 10 and at 256 divisions a single edge spanning the object needs 9, one step from silently under-subdividing and leaving holes.

The Hunyuan worker image needs rtree, though nothing imports it directly: trimesh reaches it via ProximityQuery.on_surface -> nearby_faces -> mesh.triangles_tree -> rtree, which the normal-map bake calls. Missing it in pixiecad-worker-v2 killed a job AFTER 333s of L4 generation. Now in setup_hunyuan_vm.sh and in launch_from_image.sh's check_dep self-heal (alongside fast_simplification for the paint image). Remote bake measured 45.5s at 1024 end-to-end on g2-standard-16 -- SLOWER than the 13.6s local bake; the reason to use the host is the 3.4GB of local RAM, not speed.

Hunyuan3D paint (texture) stack: bpy MUST be 4.2.x (oldest cp311 wheel; 5.x is cp312) and needs libxkbcommon0/libsm6/libice6/libxxf86vm1/libxfixes3/libxrandr2/libxinerama1/libxcursor1 even headless. basicsr needs functional_tensor->functional patched via find+sed (importing basicsr to locate it is what fails). Run the container with -w /opt/hunyuan (configs are relative to repo root) and pin realesrgan_ckpt_path absolutely. CRITICAL: end the script with os._exit(code) -- bpy teardown returns non-zero after a clean run, so a fully successful job reads as failed. 123s on an L4 for 2048x2048 PBR maps.

DINOv3 ViT-L/16 weights are secured locally. HF gate for facebook/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m is APPROVED on this account (config.json returns 200). Two copies: the live HF cache (~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--facebook--dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m) which is what any tool resolves automatically, and a purge-proof archive at ~/models/dinov3-vitl16-pretrain-lvd1689m (1.21 GB, cp -RL so no dangling symlinks, SHA256SUMS alongside: model.safetensors = dcb2e45127cccbf1601e5f42fef165eea275c8e5213197e8dcf3f48822718179). LICENSE.md from Meta ships in both. No re-request needed ever; approval also persists on the HF account. NOTE: these weights are for TRELLIS.2 only, which is NOT on the live path -- AUTO_PRIORITY puts hunyuan-remote first and it always wins.

Hunyuan3D multi-view (2mv) is WORSE than single-view 2.1 on the F1 set: 2mv merged the front wheels into a slab and gave 18 components vs 5 for single-view, which kept four distinct wheels. Swapping left/right views changed nothing, so it is not a tag-convention issue -- 2mv is built on the older 2.0 line. Default is single-view 2.1; --multiview is opt-in.

L4 spot is persistently stocked out in all three asia-south1 zones (verified twice, 2026-08-02). asia-southeast1-b has capacity. L4 quota is 1 on-demand + 1 spot in every region checked, so sweep zones for spot rather than paying ~4x for on-demand.

SSH host-key gotcha on this project: recreating a GPU VM with the SAME name often reuses the external IP, but ~/.ssh/config still pins the OLD instance's HostKeyAlias (written by gcloud compute config-ssh), so plain ssh fails host-key verification with rc=255 while 'gcloud compute ssh' keeps working -- it manages that mapping itself. Symptom before the 2026-08-04 fix: 'Backend hunyuan-remote is not available. Registered backends: [...]', which points at the wrong thing entirely. Fix: gcloud compute config-ssh. Verified the key change was benign by comparing instance ids, not by blindly clearing known_hosts.
